content_sections.body: In this lesson, focus on acknowledgement, polite disagreement, and a reason for caution. Notice how the ideas about sharing news online are linked so that the listener can follow the speaker's meaning.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: I agree that useful news should be shared, but we should check the source first. A post can look convincing even when an important detail is missing.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Prepare a three-sentence response about sharing news online. Include the lesson language, one concrete detail, and a clear link between your ideas.
content_sections.title: Guided use

items: The speaker gives no view or experience.
The speaker reaches the opposite conclusion.
exercises.prompt: Choose the statement that best matches the message about sharing news online.
Complete this Discussing different views sentence with a suitable linker: I have experience of this topic, ____ I can explain my view clearly.

Read the text: "I agree that useful news should be shared, but we should check the source first. A post can look convincing even when an important detail is missing." Then answer: What should people do before sharing news?
Give a connected response about sharing news online, then respond politely to one follow-up view.
exercises.rubric: States a clear experience or viewpoint.; Supports the main idea with a relevant detail.; Links ideas clearly and responds tactfully.

objectives: Agree or disagree tactfully in a familiar media discussion.

constraints: Keep transcript private until the first answer.
Ask exactly one question before revealing it.
Use no media; use only the supplied transcript.
listening.goal: Identify the main point and supporting detail about sharing news online.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about sharing news online. Answer one question before seeing the transcript, then listen again for the linking language.

pronunciation.goal: Use sentence stress to make the main viewpoint about sharing news online clear.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the key message about sharing news online aloud. Stress the word that carries the main contrast or new information, first slowly and then naturally.

constraints: Use at most four tutor turns.
End after the learner has supported and clarified the main point.
speaking.goal: Complete a connected exchange about sharing news online.
speaking.instruction: Discuss sharing news online with the tutor. Give your experience or opinion, support it, and respond tactfully to one different view.

constraints: Do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a supported B1 response about sharing news online.
writing.instruction: Write 5-6 connected sentences about sharing news online. Include a clear main point, a reason or example, and a tactful contrast. Submit your draft first.

title: Discussing different views
